title: Select Work with Tags
objective: Apply tags so operators can run intentional subsets without duplicating playbooks.

sourceAlignment.title: Getting started with Ansible 10 - Tags
sourceAlignment.creator: LearnLinuxTV
sourceAlignment.note: English captions informed topic alignment and timestamps. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Tags label related tasks so an operator can select or skip a subset at runtime. They are useful for maintenance workflows such as packages, configuration, or deployment.
The always tag marks setup or safety checks that should accompany tagged runs. Use it sparingly: unexpected work under always makes scoped execution harder to reason about.
Tags are an execution interface and should have stable names. List available tags before depending on them in automation or CI.
explanation.rule: Tags narrow an existing playbook; they should not create a second hidden workflow.

examples.title: Working design or automation artifact
examples.code:
- name: Update package metadata
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    update_cache: true
  tags:
    - packages
    - maintenance
examples.note: Read the structure, predict its effect, then adapt it in the assignment and terminal mission.

checks.question: Which practice best supports this lesson’s objective: “Apply tags so operators can run intentional subsets without duplicating playbooks.”?
options: Preview scope, use state-aware modules, and verify the observed result.
Hide failures and assume the target state was reached.
Store credentials beside the playbook in plaintext.
Replace every module with an unreviewed shell command.

feedback.correct: Correct—safe automation combines explicit scope, desired state, and verification.
feedback.incorrect: The reliable workflow makes scope, state, and verification visible.

lab.title: Compare tagged execution
lab.setup: Start the disposable lab with npm run lab:up, then work from /workspace in the Terminal tab.
steps: Add tags to two harmless debug tasks.
Run only one tag and observe which task is skipped.
lab.success: The requested tag runs without executing the unrelated tagged task.
